newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU single insurance market not yet a reality.
newsitem.headline: EU single insurance market not yet a reality.

text.p: Three years after the European Union scrapped its internal borders for people, services and capital, its insurance market is still to a large extent divided along national lines.
"We have no real internal market in insurance. We are failing," European Financial Services Commissioner Mario Monti told the European Insurance Committee on Thursday.
National governments were the ones to blame for the lack of progress, Monti stressed, pinning down restrictions imposed in the name of the "general good".

Despite the creation of the EU's single market on January 1, 1993, a Belgian citizen, for example, may be dissuaded from getting a life insurance policy in Britain where it is cheaper due to tax reasons.

Life insurance premiums are usually deducted from individual's income tax on the condition that the insurance firm is established in the country where tax is paid. This is despite most EU states having concluded bilateral tax treaties between themselves.
Monti threatened that the Commission would tackle the restrictions in the European Court of Justice if national capitals persisted in snubbing the EU rules.
The Commission proposed last year a narrow definition of the "general good" concept to avoid that national governments use it to justify barriers to the freedom to provide financial services.

It said restrictions aimed, in particular, at preserving the good reputation of a national financial sector or at preventing tax fraud should not discriminate against other EU companies unless justified on public policy, public security or public health grounds. Restrictions should also be "objectively necessary and proportionate".
"I am resolved that the "general good" reasoning must be very limited and strictly applied," Monti told the committee, which represents the insurance industry in the EU, in a prepared speech.
"The general good is not a general excuse not to compete," he said.
The concept is currently being discussed with the financial services industry and the national governments with the view of achieving a final definition next year.
